model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect sizes of six different language model architectures—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in order from left to right, while the vertical axis represents the effect, scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic category contains six bars, one for each model, color-coded as follows: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (medium blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (medium green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (medium pink). Error bars are present above each bar, indicating variability or uncertainty in the effect size. The bars are not sorted; they appear in the order of the linguistic categories along the x-axis. The chart shows that for most categories, the effect sizes for all models are relatively small, generally below 10, with the exception of the IE-Indic category, where several models exhibit effect sizes exceeding 20, notably mBERT-R₂ at approximately 20 and XLM-B₂ at approximately 22. In the Semitic category, XLM-B₂ shows the highest effect at approximately 20, followed by XLM-L₂ at approximately 15. The Isolate category displays the smallest effect sizes across all models, mostly below 2. The Uralic category also shows very low effect sizes, with all bars appearing below 2.
